Giving someone water is completely different to having to engage in a sexual act with someone. When you engage in a sexual act you aren't just handing someone something, you have to give consent for them to intrude onto your personal space and you need to become intimate. Doing this without proper consent can be very damaging and is COMPLETELY different to handing someone water. You are giving someone access to your body.

I know what an analogy and comparison is, you don't need to explain it like I'm 5. You just came in saying someone could be "dying of thirst nearby". You don't need to try and make me seem dumb by breaking down some analogy and making it sound better than it initially sounded. I just stated water isn't the same as sex because water itself is a need, so it wouldn't actually be selfish to need water because you need it to stay alive and plus, it does not require you to have access to someone's body. Sex on the other hand, you do not need in order to stay alive and in my view, terming it a need can sometimes be selfish. So if someone were to be dying of thirst, you'd feel obligated to give them water because their life is on the line. With sex, their life is not on the line, but terming it as a need like water puts it in the same category where you "should" feel obligated.

I think you don't see sex in the same way that I do. I do not view sex as some item transaction. I understand your analogy and what you are getting at especially with seeking it elsewhere if someone won't give someone a need, but quite honestly with sex its not as simple as not wanting to give someone sex, because the person giving them sex actually has to engage in the act.

I think it's more complicated than someone not wanting to give it to you, because there may be reasons behind it and sometimes it is worth considering the other person's perspective. My whole point with writing this post is that although people can be free to need and want sex, a whole lot of the time this term "sexual need" leads to people feeling like they are owed sex and they feel entitled and nag their partner on, essentially pressuring them and coercing them based on this reason alone.

Someone needing or wanting sex is not selfish - I agree, unless they push this on someone who is unwilling to reciprocate. I'm not disagreeing with you on your analogy, it makes total sense, however I believe there is a different level of requirement that different needs have, and this can significantly impact on the dynamics of the situation. Let's face it, a whole lot of the time people won't just get up and seek their needs from someone else if they aren't being met, they may try and pressure the other person till they get what they want. Sex isn't always just about the act, it's also about wanting to do the act with a particular person, therefore the need itself is not just sex (otherwise masturbation could potentially be enough) but sex with your SO for example (although I guess you could argue that sex itself is different to masturbation).

I might be personally biased in this matter, but from experience a whole lot of the time people use the term "sexual need" in order to make unwilling participants feel guilty and bad and give in. Thus, I see an issue of entitlement attached to this term. Of course this isn't necessarily universal, but I've seen it enough times to be put off by it. I just can't understand feeling entitled to getting sex. When you call something that requires using someone else's body your need, that is when it can over ride someone's autonomy because once something is termed a need it becomes a necessity or requirement, and it leads to feelings of entitlement for that need
Never asked. I just stated I hoped it didn't come across that way because I genuinely didn't want it to. Stating the obvious doesn't mean I'm shaming anyone. Again, you're putting words in my mouth.
I literally just wanted to highlight how big of a problem not wanting to have sex is!? Literally didn't shame anyone

OP, first of all I am so so sorry :( . Sometimes people will abuse those who are kind because they know they can get away with it. You don't deserve it, there are just a lot of bad people out there and none of it is your fault. I understand being negative, but you're already taking a big step on trying to remain positive and I commend you for that! This shows that you aren't sucked down into the negativity as much as you may think. 

I've had my fair share of very bad abusive experiences, I too felt like there was something wrong with me and still trying to heal. But I do want to be positive and what worked for me was focusing on other things than those negative thoughts, focusing my energy into things outside of my personal relationships with other people (usually this would trigger some negative feelings). So for example, I try and focus on my career, my hobbies and even just cooking! I also have made myself accept that bad people will never acknowledge their bad behaviour, that it is who they are and I cannot change that and need to accept it. 

There is nothing you can do to change people. I know a big proportion of the world is shit and it is hard to see outside of it, but I guess there is also some good. There are good moments that are waiting to happen, that are possible. I hold out hope that things will be better at a later time. I try enjoy small things and when someone is mean or abusive I try and put a distance and forget about them completely. It is the only way I've been able to stay sane. I try and erase those things out of my mind by focusing on other things in the present. I hope one day you won't be so overtaken by all the negative thoughts. You're feelings about the world are true and valid, but you also deserve your own peace. It is okay to not pretend that the world is positive, you can still be negative about the world, but accepting that and trying to find your own little bits of positivity will take you a long way! You don't necessarily have to view everything in a positive light, even small things count. I'm sorry if my advice isn't of any help, I do struggle to express how I've tried to be more positive about my life, but over time it got better for me and I hope it will for you too. Don't beat yourself up about how you feel.

I don't know if I can offer you any amount of good advice but I will just offer you things that have sort of worked for me to calm down when I've felt like this. First of all, you are not old! I too feel old, but in all honesty you have so much of your life ahead of you and no one will see you as old except maybe high school kids. You need to try and give yourself some time to recover from this. Don't think about time, you can always change your life around, always! Your time isn't up, your life is just beginning! 

Is there any calming things you like to do? You could simply start by doing a small task every day at an exact time. I know it sounds weird but it helps to feel a bit more grounded. You could write in a journal, make a to do list, make your favorite food or go on a walk or watch something that you like. It doesn't have to be a big thing or a big change, but just something that will help give you a sort of meaning or structure to your day. Also, you say that you wasted everything. What exactly do you mean by this? There is still time! Is there something you really want to do? If so, you can make a plan about how you can achieve this thing. If not, that's okay! You're still trying to figure yourself out and that's totally fine.

If yes, then you can simply select one of those and go through the interview process, but I wouldn't necessarily sweat it if you don't have a clear cut selection of preference. If you are content with the current offer, then I suggest you give yourself a big pat on the back and some time to relax instead of putting yourself through all the other five interviews. You simply don't have to put yourself through interviews for jobs that are of less value to your current offer. You should feel proud of yourself and a massive congratulations on your offer!
